points.label: Action and sequence
points.left: Paul’s argument joins baptism into Christ’s death, burial, newness of life, the old person crucified with him, freedom from sin, and being alive to God.
points.right: Paul contrasts works of law and faith in Christ, speaks of being crucified with Christ, and describes present life in relation to the Son of God who loved and gave himself.

points.label: Evidence boundary
points.left: This later passage uses Crucifixion language inside its own argument without retelling the complete Gospel event.
points.right: This later passage uses Crucifixion language inside its own argument without retelling the complete Gospel event.

payload.posture: Paul uses participation in Christ’s death within two different arguments about continuing life.

rightEvidence.title: Crucified with Christ within Paul’s argument

payload.tension: Romans organizes the claim through baptism, burial, slavery, and new life; Galatians organizes it through law, faith, self, and the Son’s self-giving.
